title: Debt Accumulation and Financial Well-Being Among Filipino Public Elementary School Teachers
tldr: Survey of 198 Filipino public elementary school teachers reveals alarming debt levels: average debt-to-income ratio of 2.3, 83% indebted to multiple lenders, and significant negative correlation between debt burden and financial well-being (r=-0.61).
problem_and_motivation: Filipino public school teachers are known to carry heavy debt burdens due to low salaries and easy access to salary loans, but systematic empirical data on the extent, sources, and impact of this debt is lacking.
approach: Survey of 198 public elementary school teachers from 10 schools in a Philippine province.
Census sampling within selected schools (all willing teachers included).
Survey instrument: Debt Profile Questionnaire (sources, amounts, terms), Financial Well-Being Scale (CFPB adapted), Financial Literacy Quiz, demographic profile.
Institutional lending data verified against sampled teachers' payroll records where available.
Statistical analysis: descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, ANOVA by debt level quartiles.
Qualitative component: open-ended questions on debt causes and coping strategies.
findings: num: Average debt-to-income ratio: 2.3 (monthly debt payments average 2.3x monthly salary).
num: 83% are indebted to multiple lenders (mean: 3.4 lenders per teacher).
num: Top debt sources: GSIS salary loans (94%), cooperative loans (72%), 5-6 informal lenders (51%), credit cards (43%).
Significant negative correlation between debt burden and financial well-being (r=-0.61, p<0.001).
Teachers in highest debt quartile have mean financial well-being score 42% lower than lowest quartile.
Debt causes: low base pay (87%), medical emergencies (64%), education of children (58%), home repairs (41%).
Majority (71%) use salary deductions for loan payments; only 29% have remaining salary sufficient for living expenses.
Coping strategies: part-time work (tutoring, selling), reliance on extended family, and additional borrowing.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides alarming empirical data on teacher debt in the Philippines (average DTI ratio of 2.3, 83% multi-indebted). The strong negative correlation (-0.61) between debt burden and financial well-being establishes debt management as a critical PFMS need. The prevalence of salary deduction-based loan payments (71%) has implications for automated debt management features in PFMS.
directly_justifies: Average debt-to-income ratio of 2.3 among Filipino teachers.
71% use salary deductions for loan payments, leaving 29% for living expenses.
Debt burden strongly predicts lower financial well-being (r=-0.61).
limits: Self-reported debt amounts may be underreported. [unacknowledged]
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domains 1.B (PF behavior) and 13.B (debt management) were flagged as highly relevant because the study focuses on debt behavior and its impact on well-being. Domain 1.A was flagged as medium relevance because literacy is measured but not the primary focus. Domain 2.C was flagged as medium relevance for informal lender usage. Domains 2.A, 2.B, 3-12, 14 were rejected as the study is a demographic survey on debt without focus on cultural mechanisms, ML, or PFMS system design.
